name: OpenAI

summary.text: OpenAI is a California-based artificial intelligence company that develops ChatGPT and other AI models. Public records checked here show it lobbies Congress through an outside firm, Miller Strategies, LLC, and holds a federal OneGov agreement with the General Services Administration (GSA) offering discounted ChatGPT access to government agencies. Microsoft announced in October 2025 a recapitalization of OpenAI into a public benefit corporation, with Microsoft holding an investment valued at about $135 billion, roughly 27 percent on an as-converted diluted basis.

facts.claim: OpenAI completed a restructuring in October 2025 in which its for-profit branch became OpenAI Group PBC and the nonprofit was renamed the OpenAI Foundation; the Foundation holds about 26% of the PBC, Microsoft about 27%, and employees and other investors the remaining 47%. All OpenAI Group PBC board members are appointed by the OpenAI Foundation, which can remove them at any time.

facts.claim: OpenAI's largest funding rounds reported in 2025–2026 were a $40 billion round led by SoftBank in April 2025 at a $300 billion post-money valuation, a $110 billion round in February 2026 led by Amazon ($50 billion), SoftBank ($30 billion) and Nvidia ($30 billion), and a round closed in April 2026 of $122 billion in committed capital at an $852 billion post-money valuation.

sources.publisher: Wikipedia (summarising press coverage; not a primary source)
sources.title: OpenAI

facts.claim: Under the October 2025 Microsoft agreement, OpenAI agreed to purchase $250 billion of Azure services, Microsoft ceded its right of first refusal over OpenAI's future cloud purchases, and OpenAI continues to share 20% of revenue with Microsoft until AGI, which must be verified by an independent expert panel. In April 2026 the two firms announced a further agreement that removed several restrictions and dropped the revenue-share clause tied to AGI.

facts.claim: The Department of Defense's Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office awarded OpenAI a one-year, up to $200 million contract for frontier AI prototype work, with the contract held by OpenAI Public Sector LLC and most work in the National Capital Region.
facts.quote: The Defense Department has awarded a one-year $200 million contract to OpenAI for the use of its artificial intelligence models. Most of the work will take place in the Washington, D.C. area.

facts.claim: In 2025 OpenAI was named a partner of the Stargate Project, a joint venture announced January 21, 2025 with Oracle, SoftBank and MGX to build AI infrastructure in conjunction with the US government.

openQuestions: Ownership: OpenAI's own recapitalization announcement and leadership page could not be opened (live site and Wayback returned fetch failures or 404). The 26% Foundation / 27% Microsoft / 47% employee-investor split comes from Wikipedia and secondary coverage (MediaPost, mlq.ai) and has not been checked against a primary filing. The Microsoft 27% figure is confirmed from Microsoft's own post.

Board and leadership: beyond Bret Taylor as chair (confirmed in a search snippet of Taylor's own statement, not a primary board page) and the July 2026 appointments of David Velez and Robin Vince, no current board list was verified. Sam Altman's formal board seat is not confirmed; he appears as CEO in the GSA release and in secondary coverage.

Funding: the February 2026 $110B round (SoftBank $30B, Nvidia $30B, Amazon $50B) is confirmed from OpenAI's post and CNBC. The April 2025 SoftBank-led round, the October 2024 round and the April 2026 $122B close are not confirmed from a primary source. The SoftBank October 1, 2026 completion and 13% stake come from secondary coverage; SoftBank's release page was seen only as a search snippet.
Defense: the CNBC and GovConWire pages confirm the $200M CDAO award. The DoD release of July 14, 2025 returned 403 and was not opened.

Federal lobbying: the Senate LDA search page confirms the OPENAI OPCO, LLC client and the Miller Strategies filings, but individual amounts were read from aggregators (Congress.wiki, receipts.report). Check the LDA filing PDFs before publishing. CNBC reports OpenAI's Q2 2026 federal lobbying at $1.2M, a record.

State lobbying: the California figures (about $140K in 2024, over $155K in 2025) come from CalMatters, not a Cal-Access record. No other state was searched. State government contracts were not searched.
Political spending: OpenSecrets and the FEC returned 403 or an unrelated committee page; no FEC committee record for OpenAI was identified, so no federal political contribution is recorded.

Litigation and regulatory action: the Musk lawsuit outcome was not verified (CourtListener and justice.gov not reachable). A July 2025 OpenAI complaint to California's Fair Political Practices Commission about the nonprofit CANI appears in search snippets only and is not recorded as a fact.

Facts sourced to the Wikipedia article 'OpenAI_Group_PBC' (ownership split, funding rounds, the Microsoft April 2026 change, the DoD $200M contract, Stargate, the Musk lawsuit outcome, and the leadership infobox) are secondary: I read only the first ~24,000 characters of that article and could not open the primary documents (OpenAI's announcements, Microsoft's April 2026 release, the DoD release, court records) to confirm them. Verify each against the primary source before approval; none has an exact quote on file.
The Musk lawsuit outcome is recorded only as a Wikipedia summary; the court docket and the jury verdict were not opened.

Could not open openai.com (company site, charter, recapitalization and leadership pages) — fetch failed or returned 403 — so OpenAI's own account of its ownership structure, board and executive leadership is not recorded here.
Could not open Wikipedia's OpenAI article, so funding totals and lead investors (SoftBank, Nvidia, others) are not recorded; the SoftBank and Nvidia links need a fetched source before they are added.
Sam Altman's role as CEO is confirmed only by the GSA release quoting him as 'OpenAI CEO'; his board seat and any other roles are unverified.
The SEC Schedule 13D/A cited on the existing a16z/Sequoia connection page could not be re-fetched here, so the a16z/Sequoia–Twitter link is not part of this entity's findings.

The Congress.wiki page is an aggregator of LDA filings; the owner should check the amounts and the Miller Strategies relationship against the primary Senate LDA database (lobbyingdisclosure.senate.gov) before publishing.
The Congress.wiki page's 'Computer Industry' sector label and total spend figures were not checked against the underlying filings.

State-level lobbying and political spending, federal/defense contracts beyond the GSA OneGov agreement, and pending or resolved lawsuits and regulatory actions were not researched in this run; the sources reachable here did not cover them.
Connections to Nvidia, Google, Amazon, Anthropic, xAI and Elon Musk were not recorded: no source opened in this run states those relationships with OpenAI.
The GSA release mentions 'Anthropic' only indirectly through a separate GSA AI page alert; that page does not state a relationship with OpenAI and was not used.
